Nevertheless, when subtraction is possible, our framework can be easily extended to handle deletions or subtracting annotations. For concreteness, we describe below how this is done on the semiring (R ≥0, +, ×). Then the update sequence consists of two types of updates: An insertion/addition (𝑅𝑢 , 𝑡𝑢 , Δ𝑢 ) updates 𝑅𝑢 (𝑡𝑢 ) ← 𝑅𝑢 (𝑡𝑢 ) + Δ𝑢 as before, while a deletion/subtraction updates 𝑅𝑢 (𝑡𝑢 ) ← 𝑅𝑢 (𝑡𝑢 ) − Δ𝑢 . In the latter case, it is required that the new value of 𝑅𝑢 (𝑡𝑢 ) must remain nonnegative. To handle a subtraction, if 𝑅𝑢 ∉ 𝑆, we simply follow the same update algorithm but replace ⊕ with −. If 𝑅𝑢 ∈ 𝑆, we update 𝑅𝑢 (𝑡𝑢 ) to 𝑅𝑢 (𝑡𝑢 ) − Δ𝑢 and recompute 𝐻𝑅𝑢 (𝑡𝑢 ) by its definition. We use derivation counting [15] to maintain 𝐴𝑅𝑢 if 𝑅𝑢 is not the root. Specifically, for each 𝑡 ∈ 𝐻𝑅𝑢 , we associate a counter 𝑐 [𝑡], initialized to 0. When 𝐻𝑅𝑢 (𝑡) changes from F to T, we increment 𝑐 [𝜋key(𝑅𝑢 ) 𝑡] by 1.
